Scotland's Ruined Castles, Abbeys & Kirks

Every site here has visible standing masonry, including ruined mansions and country houses. They're ranked for a roughly 40-guest wedding ceremony with guests flying in from North America, scored on atmosphere, event suitability, drive time from Edinburgh or Glasgow airport, nearby lodging, and things to do nearby. Star a site to add it to the shortlist. Anyone you share this page with as a Contributor or Editor sees the same shortlist and can add to it. Photos are from Wikimedia Commons, credited under each picture. The top 66 sites were checked against current sources (October 2026) for closures, ceremony permission, space and hotels. Scores further down are estimates. “Bookable now” means Historic Environment Scotland lists it as a wedding venue or the owner markets ceremonies. Ceremonies and commercial shoots at Historic Environment Scotland or National Trust sites need their permission. Private sites need the landowner's. About 400 entries, mostly small kirks and fragmentary towers, are marked “check before visiting”: their condition, exact position, or access couldn't be fully confirmed.
